column1: # Every rule the speaker's settings are checked against, and the messages for values that break
# them. Read by lithify-agent (embedded) and by the lithify command, so the speaker and the computer
# accept and refuse exactly the same values; both test suites run the cases in settings-cases.tsv.
# Columns are separated by TABS. Kinds of lines:
#   message  <name>  <text>        what a refused value says; {value} {min} {max} {choices} {option}
#   list     <max>                 at most this many entries in a list setting
#            a text value, or each entry of a list: <min>-<max> characters, each one of <chars> -
#            a class like A-Za-z0-9_- (\s is a space, \\ a backslash; * = anything but a control
#            character). <flags>: - or a comma list of empty-ok (the empty value is fine too),
#            no-leading-dash, no-space, not-reserved (none of the librespot options below)
#   network  <rule>  <min prefix>  an IPv4 address or network: at least /<min prefix>, and none of
#                                  the networks below (a fail-fast route there would cut the
#   never    <network>             never gets a fail-fast route
#   reserved <long>  <short>       a librespot option the agent passes itself, or one that stops
#                                  librespot at once: extra arguments must not repeat it
#   port     <number>  <service>   a port the speaker's own services use

column3: {value}: --{option} is set by the agent (use its setting)
{value}: not an IPv4 address or network
{value}: too large a network (/{min} at most)
{value}: a local or special address range
port {port} belongs to the speaker's own services
the web page uses this port

column1: # No CDN is there, and a route over any of these could cut the speaker off its own network.
